extracted.intended_audience: scholars, journal editors, and institutions interested in launching or supporting academic-led open access journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and persuasive examples for scholars and organizations who want to start, run, or support academy-owned (academic-led) open access journals, especially using arXiv overlay models and journal software like Scholastica.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv overlay publishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer-reviewed articles are hosted on the arXiv preprint server with DOIs designating their published status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The arXiv model enables journals to operate with virtually no production costs; Scholastica’s arXiv integration allows authors to directly import manuscripts from arXiv and link published entries (DOIs) to the arXiv versions. Use this model to minimize hosting/production overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diamond OA (free-to-read and free-to-publish) model
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate as a free-to-read and free-to-publish-in journal (Diamond open access) rather than charging APCs or subscription fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model removes author APC burdens and aligns with the goal of affordable OA. Example: Discrete Analysis described as a free-to-read and free-to-publish-in Diamond OA journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low cost / affordability
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal should be run at a fraction of the cost of traditional corporate journals; 'the cost is orders of magnitude less than that of a traditional journal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize production and operational costs by using arXiv overlays and low-cost tooling; one aim is to provide affordable OA options to counter rising APCs charged by corporate publishers (noted as increasing upwards of 6% a year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate tooling and integrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing and using the right software (e.g., Scholastica) and integrations (e.g., arXiv import) determines the success and ease of running the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools should make set-up and maintenance simple, enable streamlined peer review and publishing workflows, and provide a professional publication website quickly. Examples: Scholastica’s arXiv integration and Open Access Publishing tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined peer review and publishing process
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal must have an effective, simple-to-use peer review and publishing workflow to handle submissions and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up processes that are easy to maintain and that scale; Scholastica enabled 'a streamlined peer review and publishing process' for the example journals. Emphasize operational simplicity from setup to handling papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional web presence and reader experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a modern, professional publication website that showcases articles and links to full versions on arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good site highlights images and descriptions of articles and gives readers a modern browsing experience while pointing to the arXiv-hosted full text. Scholastica Open Access Publishing tools were used to create such sites quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board composition and capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assembling an editorial board with the right combination of reputation in the field and willingness to work is a key requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gowers: 'the only significant obstacle is getting together an editorial board with the right combination of reputation in the field and willingness to work.' Prioritize recruiting reputable scholars who will commit time to editorial duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling disciplinary gaps / appropriate journal level
rubrics_metrics.description: Target gaps in the disciplinary publishing landscape where fair OA options are lacking and define the intended 'level' (e.g., aiming at top specialist journal standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the journal to fill a clear market need (example: Advances in Combinatorics aiming at the level of Combinatorica) and advertise that ethical OA alternatives exist for that level of scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy-ownership and nonprofit governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should be academy-owned (run by scholars/institutions) to shift power back to the nonprofit sector and reduce dependence on corporate publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize grassroots scholar-led governance to promote affordable OA and enable community control of publishing priorities and pricing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Fair Open Access Principles and community networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Fair Open Access Principles and consider joining/supporting networks like the Free Journal Network (FJN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FJN offers a way to have journals run according to Fair Open Access Principles and provides support (blog, GitLab forum) and resources. Applying these principles/networks signals ethical OA commitments and offers practical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency on pricing and contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote transparency about publishing costs and contracts (e.g., exposing ‘Big Deal’ subscription contract details) to reveal the true costs of corporate publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gowers’ public-record requests and publicized Big Deal data are cited as important for increasing scrutiny over corporate costs; transparency supports arguments for academy-led alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to signal change and influence market forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Launching academy-owned journals should be evaluated on their capacity to signal discontent with current systems and influence broader policy/market shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While single journals may not by themselves change major players, they can change attitudes/behavior and contribute to larger shifts (analogy to political change); consider the journal’s potential to catalyze institutional or policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to community resources and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage community resources (guides, toolkits, networks) to plan, launch, and sustain the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available materials such as 'Welcome to the age of academic-led journal publishing' and 'The Essentials of Academic-Led Journal Publishing', and engage with FJN and other communities for practical advice and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing production and operational complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the mechanics and ongoing operations simple to reduce barriers to starting and maintaining a journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gowers: 'the mechanics of starting a new, academic-run journal are now very easy'—the main difficulty is editorial staffing, not technical setup. Favor workflows and platforms that minimize maintenance burden.
